title: performance: canary auto-detection and rollout guards for latency/throughput regressions
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: Reduce risk of silent performance regressions during rollouts by adding automated canary detection for latency and throughput regressions and fail-fast rollout guards. Implementation: - Add a new perf_canary service that pulls streaming latency/throughput histograms and tail-percentile metrics from the runtime metrics pipeline, computes baseline windows and rolling-window deltas, and applies statistical detection (bootstrap + sequential hypothesis testing) to flag regressions with configurable confidence and minimum effect size. - Implement dynamic baselining and traffic-weighted thresholds so short windows with high variance don't produce noisy failures. - Integrate a RolloutGuard controller into the rollout orchestration (operator/rollouts) that subscribes to canary signals and will: (a) pause or abort a rollout when severity crosses configured thresholds, (b) trigger automatic fallback to previous model variant or route to reserve capacity, and (c) emit structured events for audit logs. - Expose canary controls in the Console: per-route canary policy UI, per-model canary history, and a new perf-canary dashboard (latency P50/P90/P95/P99, throughput, error-rate, detection score) with links to offending traces. - Add alerting rules that create PagerDuty incidents only for confirmed high-severity detections (reduces noise) and create Slack notifications for low-severity/observability-only events. - Add extensive unit tests for the detection logic, and end-to-end performance tests in perf-canary-pipeline that run realistic workload traces (both synthetic and recorded) to validate both detection sensitivity and false-positive rate. - Docs: add docs/perf-canary.md with examples and rollout policy YAML snippets. Rollout plan: feature is behind an opt-in rollout policy. Default clusters will not enable automatic abort until metrics collection and thresholds are validated for the tenant. We validated on the perf-canary lab and on a small subset of internal customers; see CI results and release notes for details.
commits: feat(perf_canary): add detection service and API to ingest histogram snapshots
feat(rollouts): RolloutGuard controller and abort/fallback plumbing
chore(console): dashboard and UX for canary policies
test(perf): add perf-canary pipeline e2e tests with recorded workload traces
docs: perf-canary usage guide and rollout policy examples
fix(test): tighten flakiness tolerance in perf pipeline
review_conversation: Diego Rivera (2026-02-13): Nice work. Can you explain how the dynamic baseline window adapts during traffic spikes?

Asha Patel (2026-02-13): The baseline uses a weighted-decay window plus a traffic-aware minimum window; on spikes the minimum window grows to avoid reacting to transient noise — added comments and a unit test (detector_test.py::test_baseline_scaling).
Samira Khan (2026-02-15): We should avoid automatic aborts for <5% traffic canaries by default; recommend a configurable traffic-sensitivity setting. Can you add that?

Asha Patel (2026-02-15): Added traffic_sensitivity config and documented default (5%). Updated RolloutGuard to skip aborts below that threshold unless force_abort=true in policy. See commit feat(rollouts): RolloutGuard controller and abort/fallback plumbing.
Noah Price (2026-02-16): CI flagged a flaky perf test on first run. After rerun it passed; please leave a note about test determinism and add a retry on the pipeline for that job.
Asha Patel (2026-02-16): Added retries in ci/perf-canary-pipeline.yaml and extended test harness logging. Also added a perf regression acceptance test to reduce flakiness.
Diego Rivera (2026-02-17): Approve after the small nits addressed (naming + doc formatting).
release_notes:
- Introduces automatic performance canary detection for latency and throughput regressions.
- Adds RolloutGuard to pause/abort rollouts and trigger automatic fallback on confirmed regressions.
- New console dashboard and per-route canary policy UI.
- Opt-in by default; configurable sensitivity and thresholds.
- Adds perf-canary CI pipeline and e2e tests.
notes_for_ops: Enable canary ingestion in metrics pipeline: set METRICS_CANARY_ENABLED=true on metric-ingester to forward histogram snapshots to perf_canary service.
Default rollout policies do not auto-abort; customers must opt-in or set policy.auto_abort=true.
Audit logs will include structured canary events; ensure log retention meets compliance needs.
